implementation_summary: In explicit reviewed subject constructions with a following subject clitic such as wuu/way, a definite noun surface ending in the article vowel -a is expected to use the corresponding -u subject surface. This is a sentence-role rule, not a global spelling replacement.
source_evidence: Qaamuuska Af-Soomaaliga (Puglielli & Mansuur, 2012) — grammar examples include Wiilku as yeele and ninku in a subject/predicate construction
note: Do not apply in every construction. Project evidence also preserves non-u forms before focus particles, e.g. Libaaxa ayaa eryanayaa; sentence structure must control the analysis.
A noun before ayaa/baa is not automatically rewritten to a -u subject surface. This guard prevents the subject-case recognizer from collapsing distinct focus/case constructions.

source: project pronoun system plus regression testing
note: Independent personal pronouns have their own reviewed paradigm and must not be treated as ordinary article-bearing nouns by the noun subject-case generalizer.
